children: Legal & General Group plans to lay off 10% of its employees by the middle of next year, amounting to around 1,000 job losses, as part of a broader restructuring by Chief Executive Officer Antonio Simoes.

The job cuts will initially be voluntary in the U.K, the company told staff on Wednesday. They do not include the asset management business, which oversees 1.2 trillion pounds ($1.60 trillion) of investments and has its own restructuring plan. L&G has around 10,500 employees worldwide, according to the company's website.
The layoffs aim to simplify how the company operates, by reducing duplication in roles and focusing on priorities.
Since setting out a new strategy in 2024, Simoes has slimmed the company to three core divisions from four businesses previously, and has sold off non-strategic businesses such as Cala Homes.

"Since 2024, L&G has become a simpler, more focused business. These changes represent the next stage of that transformation, ensuring that our organization and ways of working reflect the business we are now building and the rapidly changing environment in which we operate," said an L&G spokesperson.
L&G said the changes will also allow it to focus on the best long-term growth opportunities.
"We recognize and take seriously the impact on colleagues and are committed to supporting our people throughout the process and consulting with our unions," the spokesperson added.
In August, L&G said it expects 2026 core operating earnings per share growth to be above the top end of the 6% to 9% target range.
